drivingQuestion: How can the baraita's 'it is a sukka' be squared with the mishna's 'it is not a sukka' for one who hollows out a stack of grain?
outcomeNote: Rav Huna's distinction is confirmed by the baraita in the first version and is itself the resolution of the contradiction in the second

segments.he: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי: הַחוֹטֵט בְּגָדִישׁ לַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ סוּכָּה — הֲרֵי זֹה סוּכָּה. וְהָאֲנַן תְּנַן אֵינָהּ סוּכָּה! אֶלָּא לָאו, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ כִּדְרַב הוּנָא. שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.
segments.en: «That is also taught» in a baraita: «One who hollows out a stack of grain to make himself a sukka, it is a sukka.» The Gemara wonders: «But didn’t we learn» in the mishna that «it is not a sukka? Rather, is it not» correct to «conclude from it, in accordance with» the opinion of «Rav Huna,» that in certain circumstances it is possible to hollow out a stack of grain and establish a fit sukka? The Gemara concludes: Indeed, «learn from it» that this is the case.

segments.he: אִיכָּא דְּרָמֵי לַיהּ מִירְמֵא. תְּנַן: הַחוֹטֵט בְּגָדִישׁ לַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ סוּכָּה — אֵינָהּ סוּכָּה. וְהָא תַּנְיָא: הֲרֵי זוֹ סוּכָּה! אָמַר רַב הוּנָא, לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁם חָלָל טֶפַח בְּמֶשֶׁךְ שִׁבְעָה, כָּאן בְּשֶׁאֵין שָׁם חָלָל טֶפַח בְּמֶשֶׁךְ שִׁבְעָה.
segments.en: «Some raised» this matter as «a contradiction» between the mishna and the baraita. «We learned» in the mishna: «One who hollows out a stack of grain in order to make himself a sukka, it is not a sukka. But wasn’t it taught» in a baraita that «this is a sukka? Rav Huna said:» This is «not difficult. Here,» where it is a sukka, it is a case «where there is a space» measuring «one handbreadth» high «along seven» handbreadths, while «there,» where it is not a sukka, it is a case «where there is not a space one handbreadth» high «along seven» handbreadths.
